page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4.8xlarge is a storage and memory-optimized instance belonging to the Local SSDs family, deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The system is built around the x86_64 architecture and features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. Accompanied by 256 GB of system RAM, it maintains an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, placing it in an optimal tier for memory-demanding infrastructure.

Hardware integration includes 7679 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Bundling high-capacity local solid-state storage eliminates reliance on external block devices for primary disk I/O, providing favorable cost efficiency and latency characteristics for high-throughput transactional tasks, with the tradeoff of ephemeral host-bound storage management.

The combination of dedicated compute cores, large RAM density, and extensive local NVMe SSD capacity makes the ecs.i4.8xlarge appropriate for I/O-intensive database systems, such as distributed NoSQL databases, transactional relational engines, search clusters like Elasticsearch, and real-time log analytics processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4.8xlarge is a storage and memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by KVM virtualization. Built on an x86_64 architecture, it incorporates 32 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 256 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. A key architectural characteristic is the inclusion of 7679 GB of high-capacity local SSD storage bundled directly with the hardware profile, alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system operates without accelerator GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By consolidating dense memory and extensive direct-attached local solid-state storage within a dedicated-core profile, the instance provides cost efficiency for environments needing predictable I/O and low-latency storage access without external SAN overhead. It is primarily suitable for distributed databases, transactional processing, search indexing, and real-time big data analytics.
